text: David Spence Thomson CMG MC ED PC (14 November 1915 – 25 October 1999) was a New Zealand politician affiliated with the National Party. Born in Stratford, he was the son of former Stratford mayor Percy Thomson and worked as a dairy farmer. During World War II, he served in the Army in the Middle East and was imprisoned as a Prisoner of War in 1942; he was awarded the Military Cross (MC) later that same year. He married June Grace Adams in April 1942, and they had one son and three daughters. In the post-war period, he chaired Federated Farmers. In 1953, he received the Queen Elizabeth II Coronation Medal. Thomson was first elected to Parliament in 1963 to represent the Stratford electorate as a National Party member and was re-elected for that seat in every election until 1978, when the electorate was disestablished. He then served two terms as the Member of Parliament for Taranaki, the replacement seat, from 1978 to 1984, when he retired. When he entered Parliament, Keith Holyoake's government was in its second term; Thomson was appointed a minister in the government's third term following the 1966 election, initially holding the roles of Minister of Defence, Minister in charge of Publicity, War Pensions and Rehabilitation, and Minister Assistant to the Prime Minister, and later became Minister of Tourism. From 1969 to 1972, during the government's fourth and final term, he served as Minister of Police and then Minister of Immigration. He won re-election in 1972 but National was unable to form a government; he served as National's Labour and Immigration spokesperson under Jack Marshall and as Justice, Police and Immigration spokesperson under Robert Muldoon. In 1975, National formed a new government, and Thomson became Minister of Justice from 1975 to 1978 and Minister of Defence and Leader of the House from 1978 to 1984, when he retired. In the 1993 New Year Honours, he was appointed a Companion of the Order of St Michael and St George for public services.
